value.text: The provided text is an excerpt from a document titled "constitution-9pages.pdf" (specifically pages 1–4) that summarizes the United States Constitution. Its main points are: • [1] The U.S. Constitution establishes a bicameral legislature with the House of Representatives and the Senate; only the House has power to impeach, both houses try impeachments requiring two-thirds approval; all revenue bills originate in the House; members are protected from arrest but cannot hold federal offices simultaneously with elected representatives. • [2] Bills must be presented to the President for signature or return within ten days (excluding Sundays); if not returned while Congress is adjourned, it becomes law unless Congress adjourns before receiving it. Orders requiring concurrence must also have presidential approval; Section 8 grants Congress powers regarding taxes/defense, commerce regulation, naturalization/bankruptcy laws, coinage, and federal tribunals. • [3] The President serves four-year terms, appoints electors based on state representation, holds the office until death or resignation, is Commander-in-Chief, can grant pardons (except for impeachment), and must receive an oath to execute the Constitution; the President negotiates treaties with two-thirds Senate approval. • [4] No person is convicted of treason except by testimony from two witnesses or a confession in open court; full faith and credit is given to public acts of other states, each state guarantees a republican form of government against invasion, and federal laws prevail over state laws requiring ratification by nine states through their conventions.
